messages:
maria: Heads-up — ran a microbench across the mixed farm and found a perf regression for seqlen=128 on a subset of A100 machines. P95 token latency increased ~2.2x after the kernel-route change yesterday. attaching quick logs below.

devon: ugh, thanks for flagging. is this the sm-detection change from the autotune branch?

maria: yeah, the change that tries to prefer tensor-core kernels when available. seems like the detector flagged TC OK, but the runtime routed to a non-TC fp16 kernel for seqlen=128.

rahul: can you paste the GPU capability probe output from that host? curious if SM capability or driver reported weirdly.

maria: pasted the snippet from the probe run:
```
GPU 0: NVIDIA A100-PCIE-40GB
SM_VERSION=8.0
DRIVER=510.73.05
TENSOR_CORES=reported
BF16_SUPPORT=1
FP8_SUPPORT=0
DETECTION_FLAGS=sm8_tc_probe=1;bf16=1;fp8=0
```

maria: then the kernel pick log for the request:
```
[route] seq=128 candidates=[tc_fp16_fast, tc_fp16_small, fp16_default]
[pick] chosen=fp16_default reason="latency_estimate_lower_for_shortseq_v2"
```

olivia: interesting — so detector says tc_probe=1 but pick falls back to fp16_default due to the latency estimator. that estimator was updated to include cache hit effects; could be the KV cache behaviour making tc kernels look worse in the model for certain batch shapes.

sam: we saw the estimator shift in numbers after the batching heuristics change. estimator uses historical per-kernel p50/p95 and a seqlen weight. may be overfitting to small-batch traces.

rahul: suspect sequence-length-dependent pipeline mismatch: tc kernels pay an up-front kernel launch overhead + different shared memory usage, which interacts badly with KV cache eviction for seqlen around 96-160. If the estimator undercounts KV cache hits, it will prefer cheaper non-TC path but actual runtime ends up worse once KV reuse occurs.

devon: steps: 1) repro on a pinned A100 with seqlen sweep 32/64/96/128/256 2) capture per-step timings (kernel launch, compute, memcpy, kv lookup) 3) compare estimator input vs observed. I can spin up a toy harness.

maria: repro trace attached (trimmed):
```
# run: ./seqlen_sweep --model small --batch 4 --pin-gpu 0
seqlen=64 p50=12.3ms p95=18.1ms chosen=tc_fp16_fast
seqlen=96 p50=14.8ms p95=22.0ms chosen=tc_fp16_fast
seqlen=128 p50=35.1ms p95=54.7ms chosen=fp16_default (regression)
seqlen=256 p50=80.7ms p95=110ms chosen=tc_fp16_fast
```

sam: wow 128 is the outlier. the p50 jump suggests a kernel that lost cache locality or pinned to a slow path. note that 256 still picks tc and is fine.

olivia: quick theory: our sm-detector sets a "tc_available" flag based on driver reported tensor core count, but we also gate some optimized kernels on a sm_major >= 8 AND a driver >= 515 due to a known cuBLAS kernel bug. here the driver is 510 so runtime may be artificially disabling some TC fast-paths even though the probe said tensor cores exist. that mismatch might cause estimator to see candidates but runtime to filter them later.

rahul: good catch. we should unify the capability decision in one place — detector should emit both raw hw features and the vetted runtime capabilities (i.e. hw_has_tc vs runtime_supports_tc). right now different layers duplicate logic.

devon: agreed. short-term mitigation: add a check in the router to avoid preferring fp16_default when a tc_candidate exists and the seqlen is in the mid-range (96-160) unless the estimator gap > 1.5x. also add a guard to prefer the candidate with better memory-behavior estimate when KV_cache_hit_rate is high.

maria: I'll open a PR with: 1) an expanded probe output (include driver_quirks list) 2) a runtime flag `runtime_tc_safe=true|false` from a centralized capability matrix 3) a small regression test (seqlen sweep) that runs on CI farm.

ci-bot: maria created branch feat/centralize-hw-capability-matrix (link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pull/824)

sam: for the autotuner, we should also record per-machine microbench results (tiny kernel-level microbench for key seqlen buckets) into the node registry so router can use empirical numbers instead of model-estimator defaults. a 3-sample probe per node shouldn't be costly.

olivia: yes — ephemeral node-level calibration is the direction. but watch out for noise; use smoothed EWMA over the last N probes. and tag probes with driver version + cuda runtime so we can invalidate when driver upgrades.

rahul: action items: maria PR + unit test (maria), devon harness + data capture (devon), sampler to add node-microbench (sam), follow-up to consolidate capability logic (olivia/rahul). I'll schedule a quick sync tomorrow.

maria: thanks all. I'll push logs and the initial diag script to the PR. tagging @devon for repro help. :thumbsup:

devon: on it. I'll try to repro across 3 different driver versions and add graphs to the PR.

maria: closing note — let's be careful with the autonomy of the estimator vs runtime hard gating. capability detection needs to be authoritative.
